notes: Reference: geographiclib Geodesic.WGS84 Inverse/Direct (about 15 nm accuracy).
qoregeo distance() rounds to 4 decimals of the unit: 0.1 mm with unit='m'.
Points uniform on the sphere (uniform in sin(lat)), not area-uniform on the ellipsoid.
Timing numbers are indicative; the machine was shared with other jobs.

random.construction: A uniform on the sphere; B = geographiclib Direct from the antipode of A on a random azimuth, offset log-uniform in [1 m, 300 km]

time_per_call_us.note: single-shot wall time per call, indicative only

equator_boundary.note: For points on the equator the shortest geodesic leaves the equator once the longitude gap exceeds (1 - f) * 180 deg; Vincenty's lambda iteration fails beyond that gap.

lat0=0.grid: 21 x 21, offsets -1 to 1 deg in lat and lng from the antipode

lat0=45.grid: 21 x 21, offsets -1 to 1 deg in lat and lng from the antipode

haversine_theory.note: short-path bounds: the sphere overestimates north-south steps near the equator and underestimates every step near the poles

bearing.note: qoregeo bearing() is the initial great-circle bearing on a sphere, rounded to 0.01 deg; the reference is the WGS-84 geodesic initial azimuth. Origins exactly at a pole are excluded.

notes: direct: the same (start, azimuth, distance) into qoregeo destination() and geographiclib Direct; error is the geodesic distance between the two end points.
roundtrip_public_api: B' = destination(A, distance(A, B), bearing(A, B, as_degrees=True)); error is |B' B|. bearing() rounds to 0.01 deg, destination() to 1e-6 deg.
roundtrip_unrounded: the same chain on the unrounded internal helpers.

timing.note: Indicative only: measured on a shared 4-CPU machine while other jobs ran. Median and min over repeats of a loop over the same pairs.
